decision_reason: BIOMDI is a real NIST software suite with C/C++ libraries and command-line tools for manipulating standard biometric interchange records, plus build/install instructions. Hold because the repository explicitly says it is no longer developed and most functionality has moved to libbiomeval; its exact historical/product-family significance and successor boundary need confirmation, and its actual LICENSE.md covers 'data' with a U.S.-only public-domain statement plus a custom foreign permission rather than the required software grant.

government_provenance.note: The README states the software was developed by NIST employees in their official duties and describes the BIOMDI project as a set of libraries and programs; the repository is in the NIST organization.

public_source.note: The public archived repository exposes code for biometric data formats, Makefiles, sub-package READMEs and sample data without credentials.

eligible_license.note: LICENSE.md is the older NIST data notice: U.S.-only public-domain language plus separate custom worldwide permission and acknowledgment conditions, not the exact OSI-approved NIST-Software grant or clear worldwide software public-domain dedication. README separately asserts U.S. federal-employee software is public domain, but does not establish worldwide rights for this code.

primary_evidence.note: README documents build/install steps and supported formats/standards, but explicitly says the software is no longer developed and most functionality moved to https://github.com/usnistgov/libbiomeval. Current use/source parity is not established; whether the older tool warrants a distinct historical Archived record rather than successor absorption needs confirmation.
